newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis ask court to reverse Netanyahu ruling.
newsitem.headline: Israelis ask court to reverse Netanyahu ruling.

text.p: Israeli opposition lawmakers and a public watchdog group went to the High Court of Justice on Monday demanding Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu be charged in a corruption scandal.

They argued it was "highly unreasonable" for Netanyahu to have escaped indictment by prosecutors on Sunday after police had recommended he be tried for fraud and breach of trust in the appointment of an attorney general.
Legal experts said chances the court would force the prosecution to press charges were slim.
Netanyahu's coalition government remained intact even after the prosecution cited "real suspicions" about his role in the appointment of lawyer and political crony Roni Bar-On.
The scandal had sidelined efforts to pull Middle East peace efforts out of deep crisis.

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat called the "Bar-On affair" an internal Israeli matter but warned Netanyahu not to take actions against Palestinians to try to divert attention from his problems at home.
Market reaction to the events could not be gauged since the Tel Aviv Stock exchange was closed on Monday and Tuesday for the start of the seven-day Passover holiday.

"This government lost its moral basis. We believe all personalities concerned should be indicted and this is the reason we are here to appeal to the Supreme Court," said leftist legislator Yossi Sarid, who filed one of three court challenges.
A former justice minister, David Libai of the Labour party, doubted the appeals would succeed.
"I don't think the High Court will overturn the conclusions of the state attorney," Libai told army radio. "The chance the appeals will succeed to force an indictment is very slim."
Prosecutors decided only Netanyahu's political ally Aryeh Deri, already facing corruption charges, should be indicted and his director-general, Avigdor Lieberman, should face further investigation.

Communications Minister Limor Livnat and Finance Minister Dan Meridor of Netanyahu's Likud party and two small parties key to the government coalition, all of whom had considered resigning, said they would remain in the government.
The main opposition Labour party called for Netanyahu's resignation, but Livnat told Israel Channel One television the important point was that Netanyahu "didn't have any criminal intentions."

Labour legislator Yossi Beilin, using Netanyahu's nickname, said: "A criminal tonight would be satisfied, a prime minister would resign and Bibi has to decide if he is a criminal or a prime minister."
Netanyahu, 47, said in a televised speech immediately after prosecutors issued their 75-page report: "The bottom line is I didn't commit any crime and the attorney general confirmed that."
He apologised for any mistakes in the January appointment, but he said the media and opposition had tried to use the affair "to overthrow the government."
A poll of 502 Israelis for Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper after the prosecutor's report found 58 percent did not think Netanyahu had to resign over the affair while 40 percent thought he did.

Hundreds of supporters of Deri's religious Shas party attacked a Channel One television crew outside Shas party mentor Rabbi Ovadia Yosef's Jerusalem home late on Sunday, hurling stones and shouting "Death to the media," the station said.
A Channel One report spurred the police inquiry into the appointment of Bar-On. It alleged Deri coerced the government into appointing Bar-On, who would then offer him a plea bargain.
Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid a public outcry that he was unqualified for the job.
